name: Forty-One Exchange
description: Forty-One Exchange (often known simply as '41' in Southeast Asia and Indonesia) is a high-speed draw-and-discard game centered on set collection. Unlike most card games where high cards are balanced by low ones, every player in 41 is chasing the exact same perfection: a hand of four cards of the same suit that totals exactly 41 points. It is a game of probability and speed, where players must quickly pivot their strategy as the cards they need are snatched up by opponents.

overview.description: Forty-One Exchange (often known simply as '41' in Southeast Asia and Indonesia) is a high-speed draw-and-discard game centered on set collection. Unlike most card games where high cards are balanced by low ones, every player in 41 is chasing the exact same perfection: a hand of four cards of the same suit that totals exactly 41 points. It is a game of probability and speed, where players must quickly pivot their strategy as the cards they need are snatched up by opponents.

history.origins: While its exact origins are undocumented, Forty-One Exchange is a staple of Indonesian social culture (known locally as 'Main Kartu 41'). it is primarily played in informal settings like schools, community centers, and local cafes as a fast-paced gambling or social game.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Gains widespread popularity across the Indonesian archipelago.
1990s: Becomes a popular 'icebreaker' game in Southeast Asian corporate and social events.
Present: Frequently featured in mobile card game apps across Asia.
history.cultural: In Indonesia, the game is often played with small stakes or as a way to determine who pays for the next round of drinks.

setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 4 cards. The remaining deck is placed in the center as a draw pile.

rules.objective: Collect 4 cards of the same suit that sum to 41, or have the highest total suit-score when the deck runs out.
rules.gameplay:
1. Turns: Players take turns clockwise.
2. Draw: A player draws one card from either the stock or the discard pile.
3. Discard: After drawing, the player MUST discard one card, maintaining a total of 4 in their hand.
4. Ending: The game ends immediately if a player reaches 41 points. Otherwise, it ends when the stock is empty.
keyRules: The 41 Rule: A perfect hand consists of an Ace (11) and three 10-value cards (K, Q, J, 10).
Discard Awareness: You cannot draw a card and then immediately discard that same card.
Winning condition: Collect 4 cards of the same suit that sum to 41, or have the highest total suit-score when the deck runs out.

strategy.basic: Commit early. If you start with two Hearts, keep those Hearts and discard anything else. Changing suits mid-game is usually a recipe for defeat.
strategy.intermediate: Watch the Discards: If you see your opponent discarding Diamonds, that means Diamonds are 'safe' for you to build as they won't be competing for the cards you need.
strategy.advanced: The Ace Bait: If you hold an Ace of a suit you aren't using, hold onto it as long as possible. This 'chokes' the game for whoever is trying to build that suit, potentially forcing them to settle for a lower score.
tips: Aces are the heart of the game. If you don't have an Ace, your maximum score is only 30 (three 10s). You must get an Ace to win.
If the deck is getting low and no one has hit 41, stop trying for perfection and focus on having the highest total in ANY suit.

scoring.description: Players collect cards of the same suit totaling exactly 41 points. High suit-score wins if deck runs out.
scoring.winCondition: First player to collect 4 cards of the same suit summing to exactly 41 points wins immediately. If deck empties, highest suit-total wins.
